reviews.text: It's not Do the Right Thing. Did not like this weird equation between the klan and the panthers, given that their cause and how they proceeded about it were completely different. The ending was horrendous. While the racist police brutality remain a prominent issue, the film almost reduces the lack of reform down to a bureaucratic red-tape thing. It's not. What is the point of trying to make this bite sized? Lee makes a point that fascism and racism remain a threat to our society. So why the choices?
Great premise with a great true story for inspiration. However, the pacing was a bit jarring, and I just never felt connected to any of the characters throughout the story.

Adam Drivers character I really like not a whole lot of depth I feel and don’t know how much this is factual to what actually happened always love the 70s drip and the dancing was good in this but not my personal favorite

Bueno, es un poco divertida a veces, pero en general la película es bastante normal. Es muy original la idea y el final es desgarrador, pero más allá de eso tampoco me emocionó tanto, aún así la veo como una buena reivindicación. Un 5.

It's a decent film I guess but I was just getting irked the whole time I was watching it. Genuinely didnt understand why they keep Ron to man the phone calls instead of just assigning Adam driver's character to all of the undercover work. I know they have to keep the black guy in the movie but by doing it this way wouldn't they be running the risk of someone noticing the difference between the two voices or god forbid one of the members of the klan happens to have eyes on the white guy while another one calls the real Ron Stallworth, completely throwing his cover. I appreciate they have to make the black guy interact with the klan for the movie to do what it says on the tin but I just have a hard time believing that an all white police force in the 70s would be willing to risk the life of one of their own for the sake of some black guy having a chat with the grand wizard on the phone. I'm sorry but they would have kicked him off the case. My other irk is that for a movie about the oppression and murder of black people in America, this movie spends so much time discussing and showcasing how hard it was to be Jewish. I'm sorry but the two aren't really comparable and honestly it just feels like forced Israeli propaganda

The montage at the end was beautiful and touching, but the film itself felt like mythologising American history and in a pretty boring way. I feel like I didn't learn anything and it was just patting the viewer on the back the whole time. Maybe Americans appreciate it; not worth watching outside the US.

Tra cappucci bianchi, telefonate surreali e Adam Driver che deve fingere di essere l’amico più razzista d’America, il film riesce nell’impresa di farti ridere e subito dopo ricordarti perché non dovresti

no fundo parece que é meio que uma propaganda pra polícia, sei lá. difícil não ter uma certa repulsa da polícia americana, ainda mais depois do caso do floyd. mas no geral é um filme instigante, com momentos bons e uma narrativa interessante

i liked it and the message it conveyed. the story was entertaining throughout but i can’t help but feel like the film lacked subtlety in it’s delivery - for example, everyone is aggressively 70s looking, everyday, as if they were all about to go out to a party
I wanted to like this movie a lot more than I did. Great concept and decent humor, however I felt like the pacing was really unnatural in a way o struggle to describe
Their this 1 star review that kinda talked how the real ron was more of a pig against the black movement but thr movie was funny so imma give it 3 instead of 5 stars

this film doesn't shy away from showing the ugliest sides of racism in the us, often at the hands of cops, but it also concludes that the only way to stop said racism is cops. it's so contradictory that it ends up being toothless. but then you remember that the real ron stalworth worked with the fbi on cointelpro, and then its anti-direct action messaging starts to make sense. all in all, it's a very fun watch! i can't say it isn't satisfying to see the nazis get played. but it remains a deeply cognitively dissonant film the second you start examining what it says.

6/10 This movie was actually good all the way up until the end. This movie has its issues like, the severity of the attack wasn’t as dangerous as I thought, they like to jump cut a lot without more dialogue like when Ron was at the imitation and the 3 guys that were in on the attack left and then it jumps to Ron driving to where the attack will be… that should raise a lot of red flags…. I also don’t like how they make these white supremacist evil, you’re telling me that the blank panther movement isn’t more violent or radical like these white supremacists? Sounds like some favoritism here. The story overall is great, some dialogue could have been better but the ending I didn’t like. They focused a lot on white supremacist that you start to wonder, where are the skeletons for the black panther movement? Anyways this movie is great story telling but don’t let this movie fool into thinking that white supremacist are evil and you should love black panthers. Both movements are terrible groups and should not be tolerated and also hear why they act this way as well.

Gostei da mistura de humor com a crítica ao racismo, principalmente porque algumas situações conseguem ser engraçadas justamente pelo absurdo, mas também bastante desconfortáveis. Apesar disso, achei que o filme não aproveita todo o potencial que tinha. Em vários momentos senti que a história fica um pouco arrastada e que a mensagem acaba sendo muito óbvia, como se o filme precisasse explicar constantemente aquilo que já estava claro. O tom também oscila bastante, e algumas escolhas de humor não devem funcionar para o público geral. Ainda considero um filme relevante e com bons momentos, principalmente pela atuação e pela mensagem, mas esperava mais. É um filme que gostei de assistir, porém não me marcou tanto quanto poderia.

Solid and enjoyable. Some really nice camera work from Spike Lee throughout and an engaging narrative. I did think that both John David Washington and Topher Grace were weak points in terms of acting though.

Assistir a Infiltrado na Klan em 2026, 8 anos após sua estreia nas salas de cinema, é olhar por um monóculo fotográfico de lente embaçada. Em menos de uma década, o zeitgest já se metamorfoseara de tal maneira que o filme de Spike Lee é, no frigir dos ovos, indesvencilhável do clima  da política ocidental de 2018 - seja para o bem ou para o mal. É facilmente perceptível ao se analisar a recepção do longa-metragem que, sobre as condições de seu primeiro lançamento, foi possível que a empreitada dos "irmãos Stallworth" reproduzida em tela potencializasse uma apoteótica comoção ideológica sobre sua audiência. O  notável valor motivacional das cenas da KKK e do Movimento Negro - as quais o idealizador justapõe mais de uma vez, consciente e ironicamente, pela montagem paralela tão querida por D. W. Graffith - são capazes de afetar ao espectador graças ao desconforto ou a empatia. Porém, não creio ser possível dizer o mesmo sobre o aparato textual e formal de sua obra. Indeciso entre representar sua aventura policial como um retrato cosmético capaz de desfrutar assumidamente do apelo psicológico de seu aspecto retro , com suas superfícies polidas e lustradas; uma homenagem direta às sensibilidades nutridas pelo cinema setentista, do split screen ao grão do filme; ou um comentário anacrônico, cru e comovente sobre a violência racial, Lee não finca-pé sobre nenhuma das oportunidades estéticas que tais possibilidades o permitem, cruzando tais iniciativas em um híbrido no mínimo mal aproveitado. Lapsos de genialidade na direção ou inventividade na montagem não conseguem ocultar uma obra fundamentada no maniqueísmo entre forças opostas - cartunizadas ao máximo na pura bondade ou maldade, arquetipizadas na estudante radicalizada de rostinho bonito e no klansman retardado bobão - que só conseguem funcionar como cosmos narrativo quando mediadas e superadas pelo ímpeto individual do good cop boa pinta. Ao mesmo tempo, questões que fujam da obviedade identitária (como a ambiguidade entre a branquitude e a etnia judaica pautada no personagem de Driver e toda a problemática do racismo como opressão sistemática e estrutural da nação branca estadunidense) são propriamente escanteadas em favor de um thriller policial que deixa a desejar, com excessão de uma ou outra sequência dinâmica na segunda metade da minutagem. Assim, Spike Lee busca filmar suas personagens diante da necessidade de atuação civil e corporativa sem, por outro lado, permitir-se explorar devidamente as ambiguidades técnicas e ideológicas de seu projeto artístico. BlacKkKlansman , sobretudo, é um filme pouco catártico e corajoso estetica e textualmente para o papel de cinema político que buscou exercer.
Nails the subject matter and tone with a rare sensitivity, but the pacing is way off. Adam Driver is excellent but John David Washington is hurt by one-dimensional character writing.

Eylül ayının ilk filmi olarak biraz daha aksiyonlu bir film izlemeye karsr verdim yoğun ve iki film izlemeli bir haftanın ardından ve BlacKkKlansman izlemeye karar verim. Bir hayli eğlendim izlerken bazen güldüm bazen de bir durumun ciddiyetinl kavradım. Filmimiz Amerika Koloradoda ki ilk polisiminizin Ku Klux Klana karşı yaptığı bir operasyonu anlatıyor. Bunu yaparken bizi güldürüyor ve 70lerdeki ırkçılığın aslında nasıl olduğunu gösteriyor.. filmin hikayesi güzel ve eğlenceli işlenmiş özellikle bir sahne var siyahi polisimiz iki tane üyeye dokununca hemen zıplıyorlar ve orada baya güldüm. Film belli bir seviyede yapılmış ve kült bir yapım olma çabasını gösterdiğini düşünnüyorum hikayesini beğensemde komik yerler olduğunu düşünsemde son 1 ay içerisinde izlediğim bazı filmler kadar geriye gidip bu film hakkında düşüneceğimi çok ta düşüneceğimi düşünmüyorum ama dediğim gibi bu film size kesinlikle 2 saatlik güzel bir keyif sunacağına dair temin edebilirim. Ayrıca john Washington abimiz ve Adam driver abimiz o sivil polis rolünü bence güzel yansıtmışlar bayıldım oyunculuklarına tabii ki şaşalı aman tanrım bu hayatımın en iyi oyunculuğu idi demiyorum ama iyiydi. BlacKkKlansman belki Spike Lee’nin diğer ve kült olan yapımı Malcolm X kalitesinde bir yapım değil belki ama gene de kendini izleren hoş komik ve mesajını güzel bir şekilde çizen bir film. Filme genel bir puan verecek olursam puanım 7/10

I found myself bothered by numerous “plot holes” and issues with the story during this, only to look it up and find out that some of the most ridiculous shit in this movie is actually real. Yes it is based on “some fo real shit” as stated in the opening of the movie, but some of these details I just couldn’t believe. Yes, Ron Stallworth actually made the mistake of using his own name when first contacting the KKK. Yes, he actually got a white detective to handle in person interactions while he spoke to members on the phone. Yes, not a single KKK member noticed that their voices were different. Yes, when David Duke came to Colorado Springs, Stallworth’s police chief actually chose to assign him (the only black man in the entire force) to Duke’s protection, and when he objected his chief actually told him that “no one else is available”. All of this seemed pretty convenient while I was watching and I was ready to hate, but it turns out all of these details are true lol. Every scene with Laura Harrier in it, is trash af I’m sorry it just is. The chemistry btwn her and JDW is just completely nonexistent. All that being said this is good enough to watch for the one time and I was entertained but it didn’t do much else for me.
nn peguei mto a visão do filme, mas veria de novo pra tentar entender. porque uma polícia totalmente racista e q odeia os negros se infiltra na ku klux klan? a mensagem do final q o filme passa eh fd

Ce film me déchire, c'est pour la bonne cause et ça passe le bon message, le film est joli, il est marquant, mais je trouve qu'il est flou dans sa narration, je le trouve beaucoup trop flou par rapport a la représentation du racisme dans la police et il fait selon moi semblant de réfléchir sur le sujet du vecteur de la libération des noirs sans vraiment en parler. Mais bon je peux pas pas aimer ce film, ça passe le bon message, cest grand public et c'est divertissant et en plus une narration appuyée qui colle bien au thème lourd selon moi, ce film en tant que film n'est que pas mal
Came for the Spike Lee, stayed for the charming and hilarious dynamic between the leading men. Really great idea that didn’t quite land the plane and felt kinda hollow and sloppy by the end.

as much as this movie had powerful statements about police brutality and institutional abuse, i believe that there were some parts of this movie that made me think they were uplifting white voices too much and not letting black voices speak enough… i feel as if spike lee probably had a more radical vision for this movie, but some people came in and neutered it to make a serious matter into a digestible sandwich for white liberals
A very well made movie that I enjoyed thoroughly. However, the parallels being drawn between the white power and black power movements are irresponsible, which is why I can't rate any higher.

J’suis pas hyper fan du film, il est bien y a pas de soucis mais je vois pas un truc révolutionnaire ou quoi que ce soit. C’est une histoire intéressante mais que je trouve un peu légère malgré la folie de celle-ci. Parcontre c’est un film qui prend position, qui n’a pas peur de dire ce qu’il pense, de ridiculiser… et je trouve ça vraiment remarquable parce que souvent on a des films qui veulent juste plaire à tous le monde en faisant croire à de la subtilité pour cacher un manque de courage comme le fait souvent Ryan Coogler (oui je le hais). Bref pas un grand film mais Spike Lee est un vrai artiste engagé.

My little brother walked in on me watching one of the klan scenes without context. Uhh I wish my arms were longer like Mr Tickle but instead of tickling I would cover his ears from all the awful things they were saying. Good movie. Great performances. Maybe it was my expectations for this movie that let me down. I feel like there was a lot more it could've delved into. However maybe I should've gone and watched a documentary to meet those expectations. Patricia was lowkey spitting facts though. God bless her soul. It kinda felt a bit like a pro-police piece while still trying to maintain a revolutionary semblance. Never mind, on second thought there IS an underlying critique of the law enforcement system and how even when there may be a well meaning individual, the system they are working in would never yield the change they are looking for. Now I wish that theme were stronger... Another thing I found weird was the parallel scenes between the klan members and the black student union members, like pray tell what are you trying to say with that? It felt very centrist-ey. But maybe I got the wrong idea idk.

Entrompe la pelicula pensando que era otra y termine viendo algo más serio de lo que pensé. Me gustó mucho los planos en el que usaron el Dolly, me parecieron acertados y precisos. Adam Driver se la lacrea siempre.
2.5 喜剧层面没有惊喜、归根结底是思考上的平庸。KKK和黑人平权两面的呈现以及中间派的表达选择都流于表面、很难想象斯派克李是一个拍了这么多年黑人电影的导演、搞得本来想补他的作品的有点被劝退了。电影正义换成影院正义是可以、靠煽动和喊口号而非寻求共情就很难懂了、创作理念和2016版《一个国家的诞生》一样让人难以接受。
Good social commentary. Just not what I was really expecting in some parts but fundamentally not a bad movie. I think I personally just wanted more out of it.

Turning the volume down during every racial slur and raising the volume for every instance of black power to show my neighbors I’m not problematic. A true Trump 1 Era movie, for both good and (some?) bad. I had the feeling Spike really wanted to make a 70’s thriller, and so much of the production, vibe, and cinematography is, but it also falls quite short. I remember the huge level of discourse related to “The main character is a cop” when this came out, and I think unfortunately despite the nuanced but radical bend it starts with it falls quite flat. Yeah sure, all your stuffy white colleagues are gonna magically get together to arrest the racist cop. I think the real story’s actual complete lack of climax is the undoing for the end of the movie, feels unearned, even if I do fuck with the montage at the end emotionally. Also I think its a shame the son of a top-3 actor of the last half century is one of the worst actors in film the last decade.

Ladies and gentlemen… Spike Lee has done it again The shot diversity in the gun range scene alone made me realise how much spike Lee put into this story. Showing the change between the truth and the kkk ‘emotional truth’ was done so effectively with the changing lighting and showing memory vs myth - literal perfection I originally thought the bar scene was a bit Hollywood full circle-y, but the ending showing the documentary footage made it all feel real. It takes us away from the comfort of this being a 1970s stories, because it’s not, the parallels are there today. Also… you can’t convince me that Adam driver isn’t Jewish, that man drinks matzoh ball soup like juice

Technically a rewatch but it’s been a close to a decade. This is Spike’s anti-Trump protest joint, and what he does well in it is showcase how the same slogans/figures of speech/dynamics of power that have defined black oppression in this country for decades are very much still at the forefront of our political consciousness. The same old gangs are saying the same old shit that they’ve been saying for generations. He is not subtle about it, at all. What he doesn’t do well is make a tonally consistent film. This thing is all over the place, man. The best parts are the final 2 mins of “real” footage inserted at the end, and that absolutely filthy guitar riff that plays over and over throughout the runtime. Oh and also the hallway dolly shot YES Spike YES!!!!

Segunda película que veo de Spike Lee, segunda decepción que me llevo. Sinceramente no tengo demasiado que reprocharle, no me parece una mala película, puedo apreciar perfectamente lo que hace, pero al igual que me pasó con Inside Man, terminé la película pensando que me gustó más lo que Spike Lee quería decir, que la película que hizo para decirlo. BlacKkKlansman está cargadísima de problemáticas sociales y raciales, o sea, ésta directamente gira en torno a una historia real sobre la secta racista más conocida de la historia. Y claramente banco el mensaje, la crítica y lo absurdo que resulta todo esto. El tema es que la película nunca me llevó un punto más allá. La premisa es cuanto menos entretenida de ver, y tiene situaciones que en el papel deberían ser tensísimas o incómodas, pero en ningún momento percibí que la película llegara a explotar realmente. Todo avanzaba y rara vez sentía que algo tuviera verdadero peso, incluso la historia termina siendo bastante predecible. Y aunque no tengo ningún problema con los finales felices, este me pareció demasiado hollywoodense para tratarse de una historia basada en hechos reales. De hecho, el cierre terminó de confirmarme esa sensación, ya que en vez de sentir que la película había llegado naturalmente a un punto de quiebre, sentí que Spike necesitaba detenerse para recordarme cuál era el mensaje que acababa de ver durante dos horas. Tal vez también tengan algo que ver las expectativas. Ya que ésta, junto a Malcolm X y Do the Right Thing son películas que llevaba muchísimo tiempo queriendo ver, y entre las críticas y todo lo que se escucha sobre ellas, terminé llegando con las expectativas por las nubes. Esperaba que esto me demostrara por qué Spike Lee ES Spike Lee, pero no pasó. Aún con todo esto, le tengo una fe increíble a las otras dos.

C’est pas le genre de film que je regarde, je suis pas fan des trucs policiers, mais là le sujet est important. On voit l’oppression des personnes noires et l’abomination qu’est le Ku Klux Klan. Les vidéos à la fin qui proviennent d’événements réels si récents (2017) montre que les noirs seront toujours oppressés. C’est répugnant de voir un racisme si banalisé envers des membre de notre même espèce humaine. J’apprécie les films parlants de sujets importants comme celui-ci, il faut continuer d’en faire pour montrer aux gens que des personnes horribles comme le KKK existent encore et qu’il faut changer les choses.

this is brilliant. so many incredible shots, john david washington and adam driver are fucking electric. Maybe I’m calling for the death of subtlety but i do wish the movie made it a bit more obvious that Ron is actively making the wrong decision by staying on the force. the fact that, even after he resigned from the kkk, he was still a black klansman is the most fascinating juxtaposition in the movie, i would’ve loved to see it explored more. but maybe i missed something. regardless, absolutely phenomenal. EDIT: Upon reading more on Spike Lee’s intent with this film, it seems that Ron’s choice in the end wasn’t even intended to be thought of as wrong. that’s really disappointing, i think this movie could’ve made a really important and meaningful point but it chickened out in the end to be more palatable. i have to take my rating down a bit, even though the first 90% of this film is truly incredible.

Vraiment très très propre! Pas grand chose à dire. Le film est vraiment bien est dénonce de vraies choses. En plus de ça, les images réelles montraient à la fin sont horribles mais ils fait que les gens les voient pour vraiment comprendre les problèmes de la société.

L’histoire est horrible les images à la fin sont absolument choquantes et ça parle d’un sujet très important mais en soi le film n’est pas si innovant que ça en tout cas ça reste quand même un film très important

I can't really ignore that this is copaganda. We are meant to sympathize with the struggles of our main character when his girlfriend challenges him and is very upset when she finds out that he's a cop, because she just 'doesn't understand'. He actively combats her on her beliefs repeatedly, and I felt that the story was painting her as ignorant and not understanding of how much the police system of America exploits black suffering. It completely invalidates and sidelines the fact that the justice system in America, especially during that point in history, was extremely racist and often negatively black and impoverished communities. We are meant to see Ron's girlfriend, Patrice, as some radical who just can't see past her pig hating lenses and trust her well meaning cop boyfriend, who only wants the best for their people. She even seems to ease up at the end of the movie, which is fine since the man that assaulted her was going to be punished for his crime, but it seems unfaithful to her original character. One of the biggest critiques people have of America's justice system, racism aside, is that it doesn't rehabilitate — it punishes. This seems ideal when you consider that pedophiles and other offenders of violent crimes will suffer, but it doesn't account for the fact that people like thieves and loiterers are also in there suffering. Some people think it's adequate, but it doesn't actually do anything proactive to prevent crime and often causes more issues than solutions. This is often something socialists and pro black activists complain about, and during the Black Panther era, dismantling the prison system was very, very important to their politics. Although I definitely believe that degenerate deserved to suffer for what he did to Patrice, the Patrice we know at the beginning of the story wouldn't abandon her political beliefs for any one at any time, not even for her boyfriend. This means, that in some attempt at character growth, Patrice abandons her politics and trusts the police officers at the end of the story. Hm. It's almost like the writers wanted to paint the police as heroes and convince those watching that movements like the pro-Black movements need police officers to keep them safe. The movie is meant to make us feel like you can fix the system from the inside, and it humanized police officers and the system in a way that made them feel more like victims than perpetrators. Cops are not your friends. Other than that, the movie was pretty good. The actors did a phenomenal job, shed some light on the KKK and how these racists paint themselves as charismatic to fool the population and seem more reasonable than they truly are. It definitely had its good sides, and its funny moments. Just wish they toned it down on the police dick riding.
